public_rationale: Stanford's retrospective comparison shows substantial narrowing across language, mathematics and coding benchmarks during 2024, before Marcus's post. DeepSeek's December 2024 report provides contemporaneous corroboration. These results support 'catching up'; they do not establish Chinese leadership across every capability or across the wider AI industry.
limitations: Benchmark performance does not capture every aspect of real-world reliability.
The main comparative report was published after the post but measures pre-post outcomes.

statement.document_title: Hot take on an AI catfight

our_interpretation: Read as narrowing the capability gap between leading Chinese and U.S. language models, not claiming that China already led.
Use comparable language, coding and mathematical-reasoning benchmarks as ordinary measures of LLM capability.
Assess the latest models available before the post and the preceding year's trend, using earlier results as the baseline.
Later publications may establish historical results, but post-January 22, 2025 model improvements do not count.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable evaluations show that leading Chinese models materially narrowed their performance gap with leading U.S. models across several relevant benchmarks by the post date.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evaluations show no meaningful narrowing, or a widening gap, across the relevant capability measures during that period.

evidence.explanation: The preceding sentence gives end-2023 U.S.–China gaps of 17.5, 13.5, 24.3 and 31.6 percentage points on MMLU, MMMU, MATH and HumanEval. All four narrowed by end-2024, including the language, mathematics and coding measures directly relevant to this claim.

The contemporaneous report corroborates that a leading Chinese model had approached leading closed-model performance before the post. It is developer-reported evidence and is secondary in weight to the cross-country benchmark comparison.
